title: Magic Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Kathleen Chang, Anasuya Lyons, Yuanjie Ren, Harald Putterman, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Victor V. Albert, Benjamin J. Brown, Dominic J. Williamson
abstract: Non-Clifford operations required for universal quantum computation can be implemented by measuring logical Clifford operators. We present a generalized framework to fault-tolerantly measure transversal Clifford logical operators in quantum low-density parity check (QLDPC) codes. Our protocol takes any QLDPC code and deforms the code across additional ancillary qubits such that a product of stabilizers measures the desired logical Clifford operator. We prove that the deformed, Clifford-stabilized code remains LDPC and that its distance is preserved up to a constant factor independent of the number of physical qubits. We further prove that the Clifford measurement has a fault distance against data qubit and measurement errors that grows linearly with the distance of the original code. We apply our methods to implement logical non-Clifford gates in algorithmically relevant subroutines and to prepare magic states in quantum stabilizer codes.
summary: This paper introduces a general, fault-tolerant framework for measuring logical non-Clifford operators within QLDPC quantum error-correcting codes. By 'gauging' the code structure across ancillary qubits, the authors construct a new code whose stabilizers allow for the measurement of the desired logical gate. This method preserves the code's distance and ensures fault tolerance, providing a pathway to universal quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of fault-tolerantly measuring logical non-Clifford operators, which are necessary for achieving universal quantum computation using QLDPC codes.
main_result: They present a generalized, fault-tolerant framework that deforms the QLDPC code across ancillary qubits to measure the desired logical Clifford operator, preserving the code's distance up to a constant factor.
method: The core method involves a 'spacetime gauging procedure' where the original QLDPC code is augmented with ancillary qubits to create a gauged code ($\mathcal{C}'$), whose stabilizers are measured to realize the logical operation.
model_or_system: The system studied is the Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) code, generalized to modular q-ary qudit codes. The process involves constructing a 'gauged code' ($\mathcal{C}'$) by deforming the original code structure.
key_observables: Fault distance (which grows linearly with the original code distance), the distance of the gauged code ($d_g$), and the resulting logical Clifford operator measurement.
important_parameters: The code distance ($d$), the number of physical qubits ($n$), and the order of the operator ($p \geq 2$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the ability to perform local measurements that deform the code structure, and some proofs are cited as being informal or requiring further work for specific operators ($p>2$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the spacetime protocol for gauging, showing the structure of the gauged code $\mathcal{C}'$, the resulting stabilizers, and the fault tolerance analysis.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the general gauging framework, proves that the resulting code remains LDPC with preserved distance, details the fault-tolerant measurement protocol, and applies these methods to prepare magic states and implement non-Clifford gates.
why_interesting: The rigorous development of fault-tolerant measurement protocols for non-Clifford gates is a cornerstone requirement for scaling up quantum computation beyond current NISQ devices.
